name: Purple Orach
family: Amaranthaceae, the amaranth and goosefoot family
grown_as: Red garden orache, an annual grown for its young leaves (eaten like spinach) and as a tall ornamental. Often self-sows. William's records give no variety.
habit: A tall, upright, branched annual 1 to 1.8 m with a stout purple stem, narrow and spire-like. Picked young as a leafy plant 20 to 40 cm.

leaf.outline: Triangular to arrow-shaped, 5 to 15 cm long, smaller and narrower up the stem
leaf.base: Straight across or arrow-shaped, the two lower corners pointing outwards
leaf.margin: Smooth to slightly wavy, sometimes with a few shallow irregular teeth
leaf.veins: A midrib and few side veins, not prominent
leaf.surface: Soft and thin; young leaves with a fine glistening mealiness, later matt

flower.form: Tiny flowers without petals in long branched spikes; the female flowers sit between two flat, round bracts which become the showy seed discs
flower.centre: Tiny stamens on the male flowers
flower.behind: A pair of flat, round, papery bracts round each female flower, growing to 1 to 1.5 cm
flower.carried: In long, slender, branched spikes at the top of the plant and in the upper leaf joints, upright then arching
flower.size: Flowers about 1 mm; the bract pairs 1 to 1.5 cm

fruit: Dense hanging spikes of flat, round, papery discs like small coins, each a pair of bracts round a single seed, purple fading to buff-brown. The seed inside is flat and round, 2 to 3 mm, brown or black.
seedling: Two narrow strap-shaped seed leaves, purple, then small triangular purple true leaves.
winter: Nothing: an annual. Dead brown seed spires stand into winter and drop self-sown seed.

bloom: each female flower between two flat round purple bracts
seed: a flat round papery disc about 1 cm with a seed in the middle
the seed itself flat, round, brown or black
seedling: two narrow strap-shaped purple seed leaves
the first true leaves triangular and purple
young: a small upright purple plant with triangular leaves
crop: a leafy upright plant 20 to 40 cm, deep purple all over
flower: a tall narrow spire 1 to 1.8 m with a purple stem
long branched purple spikes at the top
seedhead: long drooping spikes crowded with flat round papery discs

look_alikes: Green orache is the same plant without the purple. Fat hen has mealy, toothed, grey-green leaves and no seed discs. Red amaranth has oval leaves and furry tassel-like flower heads. Beetroot leaves are purple-veined but glossy and on a swollen root.
